§12.2.2 Diagrams and Flowcharts

📄 Page rule — applied from the page alone

diagrams-diagrams-and-flowcharts · rule diagrams

✅ Normative

A diagram or blueprint MUST use a fenced diagram/<language> block when a suitable language can faithfully represent its content. If no suitable language can do so, the output MUST use a fenced description block. A diagram that is really tabular SHOULD be rendered as an HTML table. A diagram MUST NOT be left out of the output.

Fence and language selection

The opening fence MUST identify the language actually used: diagram/mermaid, diagram/plantUml, diagram/dot, diagram/tikz, diagram/svg, diagram/circuitikz, or another suitable diagram/<language> tag. The suffix is case-sensitive; plantUml is the canonical PlantUML spelling. diagram/<language> is a pattern, not a literal tag. Bare mermaid, plantuml, diagram and diagram/text MUST NOT be used for diagram output.

The producer SHOULD use the following priority order, considering only languages that preserve all the figure's content. A higher-ranked language MUST NOT be used if doing so loses information. Different figures in one document MAY use different languages. An unlisted language MAY be used when it preserves content the listed choices cannot. The order is a protocol preference, not a claim that every language supports every figure in that row.

Figure type Preferred languages, in order Content that decides suitability
Flowchart, process, organisation chart Mermaid → PlantUML → Graphviz DOT → TikZ → SVG Labels, branches, arrow directions, grouping
UML, sequence, class, state, ER diagram PlantUML → Mermaid → Graphviz DOT → TikZ → SVG Diagram-specific symbols, relations, multiplicity, message order
Functional block, system or network diagram Mermaid → PlantUML → Graphviz DOT → TikZ → SVG Blocks, ports, signal paths, nesting; positions when meaningful
Dense dependency graph or tree Graphviz DOT → Mermaid → PlantUML → TikZ → SVG Complete nodes, edges, directions and clusters
Blueprint, floor plan, geometric or spatial schematic TikZ → SVG Walls, openings, geometry, orientation, dimensions and label placement
Component-level electrical circuit CircuiTikZ → TikZ circuit libraries → SVG Component symbols, pins, junctions, wire crossings, topology and orientation

Mermaid and PlantUML MAY represent a conceptual room-relationship diagram when its content is only nodes and connections. They MUST NOT replace a spatial floor plan with an automatically arranged graph that loses walls, openings, geometry or dimensions. A language being called “architecture” does not make it a floor-plan encoding.

The block body MUST be valid in its named language. Every printed label, connector, direction, meaningful grouping and spatial feature MUST be preserved, without adding inferred content. Internal identifiers and drawing coordinates are encoding, not additional printed measurements; coordinates MAY follow visible geometry but MUST NOT be presented as measured real-world values. Printed measurements MUST be copied verbatim even when inconsistent.

Description fallback

When no suitable language can faithfully encode the figure, the output MUST use a fence whose entire tag is description, not diagram/description or diagram/text. The body follows the fixed shape in Slide Diagrams§12.2.5, Blueprints§12.2.1 or Electrical Schematics§12.2.3: printed title if present, what is visibly shown, labels and their visible features, then values and notes. It MUST preserve all legible text and describe visible structure without guessing hidden connections, measurements or domain meanings. Difficulty alone does not justify replacing an encodable diagram with a description. The fallback examples below and in the specialised notes illustrate this case; they do not require descriptions when a faithful encoding is available.

Charts, geographic maps, chemical formulae and music retain their specialised content rules.

```diagram/mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[Application received] --> B{Complete?}
  B -->|Yes| C[Underwriting]
  B -->|No| D[Return to applicant]
```

Preserve spatial and domain meaning

Automatic graph layout is suitable when connections carry the meaning. Where positions, orientations or physical topology matter, the chosen language MUST preserve them. Floor plans follow Blueprints§12.2.1, circuits follow Electrical Schematics§12.2.3, maps follow Geographic Maps§12.2.4, and structural formulae follow Chemical Molecules§13.1. A successful render alone does not show that an encoding preserved the source.

Labelled conceptual diagrams

When no suitable language can faithfully encode a labelled conceptual figure, it is rendered as a fenced description block that names each element and what is visibly drawn there, so a chunker keeps the labels together — see Slide Diagrams§12.2.5:

```description
## Detector cross-section
- **Anode**: top grid
- **S2**: secondary scintillation, produced in the gas phase
- **e<sup>-</sup>**: electrons drifting upward through the liquid
```

Examples

✅ Sample — an organisation chart

A staffing chart: boxed roles connected by rules into a strict hierarchy, five departments across the top and two separate contracted-services blocks below.

This is the case Mermaid is for. The content is entirely nodes and edges — who reports to whom — and none of the meaning lives in where a box sits on the page. Redrawn by a layout engine it would still say the same thing, which is exactly the test that a circuit or a floor plan fails.

Two things are easy to lose and MUST be carried across: the numbered suffixes distinguishing repeated roles (事務員①, 事務員②), and the annotations inside or beside the boxes (週29H, 週1×4H) — those are hours, not decoration, and they belong to the node they sit with. Each bracketed department label (＜管理課＞) names the group above it and becomes a subgraph title. Edges follow the printed rules: each department head connects by a rule to the stack of roles beneath it. The two lower blocks print no connecting rules, so their roles are grouped without edges. Expected boxes: the title line, and the chart as one Picture box.

## Language references

The preference order above is a protocol choice informed by the documented language capabilities:
[Mermaid diagram types](https://mermaid.js.org/intro/syntax-reference.html),
[PlantUML diagram types](https://plantuml.com/),
[Graphviz DOT](https://graphviz.org/docs/layouts/dot/),
[TikZ coordinates](https://tikz.dev/tikz-coordinates),
[SVG](https://www.w3.org/TR/SVG2/Overview.html), and
[CircuiTikZ](https://circuitikz.github.io/circuitikz/).
